newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA sees little need for early policy action.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA sees little need for early policy action.

text.p: Official forecasts for the Australian economy in 1996/97 (July-June) suggested little need for early monetary policy action, Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Bernie Fraser said in Tokyo on Thursday.
However, the forecasts were subject to risks and for that reason policy was under constant review, he told a business seminar in Tokyo. A copy of his speech was released in Sydney.
Fraser said that in this monitoring, policy makers would be alert for any early signs of significant changes in business investment, wages growth of unemployment.

"Unemployment aside, the official forecasts for 1996/97 look fairly comfortable, indicating as they do another year of three percent growth and two to three percent inflation," Fraser said. "At face value, they suggest little need for early monetary policy action," he said.
Fraser said that the RBA was aware of the many risks -- in both directions -- these forecasts were subject to, and therfore the need to keep policy under constant review.

"Policy makers understand these risks, which is why policy remains under constant review; in their monitoring of economic developments, policy makers will be alert for any early signs that business investment or wages growth or unemployment, for example, might be diverging significantly from the current forecasts," he said.
The Reserve Bank cut official interest rates by 0.5 percentage points to 7.0 percent on July 31, the first interest rate cut in three years.
